FTGhQcpG_RA.description:
You press a finger against glass and feel a surface. There is no surface.

Atoms have no edge. What stops your finger is the Pauli exclusion principle.

Sources:
https://van.physics.illinois.edu/ask/listing/64449
FTGhQcpG_RA.title: You Have Never Touched Anything

TEipugAb-GE.description:
Cover one nostril and breathe. Now swap sides. One of them is moving most of your air, and the other has been narrowed — not by a cold, not by a deviated septum, and not by accident.

This is the nasal cycle. Erectile tissue on your turbinates fills with blood & swells inward on one side while the other side opens.

Sources:
https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0162918
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12938-015-0034-4
TEipugAb-GE.title: Your Nasal Cycle Narrowed One Nostril On Purpose

Hold your palm up right now. Touch your thumb to your smallest finger, bend your wrist forward, and count the cords that stand up. Most people see two. Some see one.

Sources:

cbUPlcHJSFs.title: You Might Not Have A Palmaris Longus Muscle
